Core read: The Fed sees activity picking up and the labor market strong, but inflation broad-based and elevated; policy is decisively hawkish with a 75 bp hike and balance-sheet run-off. SLOOS cross-check: Domestic banks on net eased standards for C&I and multifamily loans and kept construction and nonfarm nonresidential standards largely unchanged; they reported stronger demand for HELOCs and auto loans but weaker demand for residential real estate loans, and eased standards on credit cards. Foreign banks, however, tightened C&I standards. Implication: Despite the Fed’s tightening and elevated vulnerabilities, domestic credit supply to businesses and some consumer segments remained accommodative, cushioning near-term growth, while housing shows early cooling and cross-border lending is a headwind. Netting these, the overall tone shifts from moderately negative toward slightly negative.
